current_platform_notes: Supabase now requires explicit grants for new public-schema objects before Data API exposure.
RLS remains separate from Data API grants and must be enabled and forced on exposed multi-tenant tables.
Database functions default to PUBLIC execute and must be explicitly revoked when privileged.
Security invoker remains preferred; any security definer use requires a private schema, empty search path and explicit caller check.

blocking_findings.finding: The R5 receipt scope binds owner and subject but omits the canonical Brain workspace.
blocking_findings.risk: The same subject can participate in personal, company and project workspaces, so owner and subject alone cannot establish tenancy or context authority.
blocking_findings.required_repair: Add workspace_id to every receipt, event, command, projection, encryption context and test.

blocking_findings.finding: R2 through R5 use customer_private and operator_private while the live Brain uses person_private and delivery_team_private.
blocking_findings.risk: Persisting both vocabularies creates ambiguous policy and invites accidental widening.
blocking_findings.required_repair: Use the canonical Brain audience vocabulary in persistence and make presentation-language mapping explicit at the adapter boundary.

blocking_findings.finding: brain_audience_grants stores purpose, but current Brain SELECT policies match workspace, user and audience without comparing grant purpose to row purpose.
blocking_findings.risk: A grant for one purpose can currently satisfy a read of the same audience under another purpose.
blocking_findings.required_repair: Prove exact purpose matching in a separate canary before prepared-intelligence content relies on the Brain read boundary.

blocking_findings.finding: R2 through R5 correction dependencies are opaque tokens rather than typed, version-bound references.
blocking_findings.risk: A correction cannot safely invalidate a receipt if the reference does not identify the authoritative table, record version and fingerprint it depended on.
blocking_findings.required_repair: Replace opaque context refs at the persistence boundary with typed dependency receipts for Brain item versions, decision cases, decision claims and external source receipts.

blocking_findings.finding: The strict Brain cipher supports source, assertion, item_version and relationship_version only.
blocking_findings.risk: Reusing source would blur semantics; storing prepared content without a dedicated authenticated-encryption context would weaken row and field binding.
blocking_findings.required_repair: Add and test a prepared_receipt record kind and payload field only after the persistence scope is accepted.

route_comparison.reason: Keeps receipts subordinate to workspace, audience, purpose, correction, retention and erasure authority while allowing payload-free events and encrypted content.
Current purpose enforcement is incomplete and the source record kind does not faithfully describe a prepared-intelligence receipt.

route_comparison.route: Use briefings or delivery tables as authority
route_comparison.reason: A delivered artifact cannot become the truth source for the evidence and Brain state that produced it.
It would become a second Brain with parallel tenancy, correction, retention and erasure policy.

preferred_future_shape.receipt_table: A Brain-owned receipt envelope with workspace, subject, canonical audience, exact purpose, kind, content fingerprint, encrypted payload, produced and expiry time, current invalidation and erasure projection, and opaque idempotency key.
preferred_future_shape.dependency_table: One row per typed, version-bound authoritative dependency with real foreign keys where possible and exactly-one-target constraints.
preferred_future_shape.event_table: Append-only payload-free accepted, invalidated, erased and delivery-reference events with actor, authority and exact before or after fingerprints.
preferred_future_shape.projection_table: Optional rebuildable prepared-object cache bound to exact receipt IDs; never canonical Brain truth.
preferred_future_shape.atomic_boundary: One short security-invoker transaction callable only by a narrowly granted backend role after external work and encryption complete.
preferred_future_shape.read_boundary: A non-anonymous user-scoped read that must satisfy active workspace membership and exact audience plus purpose grant before server-side decryption.
preferred_future_shape.delivery_boundary: Existing briefing, audio, email and export organs consume a current prepared object but never update receipt truth.

required_database_proofs_before_executio: fresh isolated schema syntax and migration test
four-identity RLS matrix including anonymous-auth rejection
conflicting replay rollback with no partial rows
correction event plus receipt and projection invalidation in one transaction
erasure content removal and payload-free audit readback
all foreign-key and RLS lookup columns indexed
security and performance advisors clear or explicitly adjudicated

authority.allows: Local contract repairs, fixtures, tests and a later reviewed migration proposal.
authority.forbids: Migration file, database branch, database write, function deployment, runtime caller, production action, merge or legacy retirement.
